story.what_it_does: Polycab makes wires and cables, its biggest business (about ₹252 billion of FY2025-26 revenue). It also sells fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG) such as solar products, and runs a smaller EPC (project execution) business. Exports are only about 5% of revenue.
story.plans: Management targets an FMEG EBITDA margin of 8-10% and a 10% export share of revenue by FY30. It also targets a 30% dividend payout and a capex programme of at least ₹60 billion over five years, including an EHV plant due around FY28.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a moat directly. They show scale (record revenue of ₹288.8 billion in FY26), a net cash position of ₹45.2 billion, and wires & cables margins of 14%+ in recent quarters. A new competitor, UltraTech, is entering wires, and channel checks suggest it prices 10-15% lower.

scenarios.story: Revenue keeps growing fast (Q2 FY27 up 53%) while margins hold near 14% and FMEG reaches its 8-10% margin goal early (10.1% EBIT in Q2). Net cash stays strong and the capex plan adds capacity such as the EHV plant.
signals_to_watch: FMEG EBIT margin staying around or above 10% after the Q2 FY27 record of 10.1%
Wires & Cables margin staying within or above the 11-13% guided range (14.2% in Q2 FY27)

scenarios.story: Growth stays healthy but slows as copper-driven price effects and a very high base fade, with margins around 13-14%. Exports stay weak while geopolitical issues continue, and working capital drifts back toward 45-50 days.
signals_to_watch: Working capital cycle moving from 11 days toward the expected 45-50 days
Cable and wire volume growth, which was only low to mid single digits in Q1 FY27

scenarios.story: Falling copper prices cause channel destocking and the new low-priced competitor in wires squeezes pricing, while exports stay hit by Middle East and US tariff issues. Strong recent revenue growth may have come partly from copper-led price rises and stocking rather than lasting demand.
signals_to_watch: UltraTech's pricing, with competitor prices reportedly 10-15% lower
International revenue, which fell 13% in Q1 FY27, and export bookings hit by shipping delays
